name: Lemon bottle

lead: Lemon Bottle is a brand of lipolytic (fat-dissolving) injection promoted on social media. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to reduce buccal fat, jowls and submental fullness for a leaner face.

Opinions differ on forums: some users say other products such as Aqualyx work better, while others say it keeps the face "debloated". Forum posts also cite a claim that a Swiss health agency found listed ingredients missing from tested products.

paras: Discussion describes a clinic-administered or self-administered injection into fat areas of the face. No dosing or technique is given here.
Injections near the face carry risks including swelling and nerve or vessel injury; users themselves ask about nerves. Product contents have been questioned in forum posts.

chain: Fat reduction in the cheeks or jowls
angle.text: Users hope the injection thins buccal fat and jowl fullness. Reports of results are anecdotal.

lead: Lemon Bottle is a brand name for an injectable fat-dissolving solution popular in Turkey and promoted through social media. In looksmaxxing forums it is raised as an option for facial slimming around the cheeks, jowls and under the chin, and for body areas such as love handles [1][2][3][4].

Users compare it with other lipolytic products such as Aqualyx and Lipolab, and some report using it themselves [1][2]. Threads also discuss the product's marketing, with one noting that a promoter's channel had grown quickly, and one cites a report that a Swiss health agency analysed several Lemon Bottle solutions and did not find ingredients from the label [3][5].

Injection lipolysis in general uses substances such as sodium deoxycholate, sometimes mixed with phosphatidylcholine, in mesotherapy. The only fat-dissolving injection approved by the FDA for the chin area is deoxycholic acid (Kybella, approved in April 2015); Lemon Bottle is a different product [6].
infobox: Buccal fat, jowls, submental fat, body fat (as described by users)

paras: One user planned Lemon Bottle or Aqualyx for buccal fat and jowls, asked whether anyone had done it, and asked about nerves in the area; a reply suggested pinching the jowl to see whether it feels like fat and a second recommended researching which product is best, naming Aqualyx [1]. Another user described injecting it into the cheeks and under the jaw to stay "debloated" and said their bone structure was good; replies recommended Aqualyx or Lipolab instead, and one reply cited a Reddit comparison claiming it affects lymphatic fluid [2].
Other threads ask whether it works for love handles and whether the product should be kept to a small circle for face fat [4][7].

A forum thread title states that Switzerland's health agency analysed multiple Lemon Bottle solutions and did not find an ingredient from the ingredient list [5]. A separate thread on what is actually inside the product features discussion of the promoter's marketing and the source of claims about its contents [3].

Deoxycholic acid is sold as Kybella and Belkyra, is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe fat below the chin, and a generic became available in the U.S. in April 2021. Sodium deoxycholate with phosphatidylcholine is used in mesotherapy injections [6].
No studies found for Lemon Bottle. For context, deoxycholic acid, a different injectable, is FDA-approved for reducing fat under the chin [6].

lore.intro: Lemon Bottle is discussed on looksmax.org as one of several fat dissolvers, with views split on whether it is the one to use [1][2][3].

claims.claim: Lemon Bottle keeps the face permanently debloated.
Other dissolvers such as Aqualyx work better.
Its listed ingredients do not match contents.

timeline.event: FDA approves deoxycholic acid for fat below the chin, a different product category from Lemon Bottle [6].
Generic deoxycholic acid becomes available in the U.S. [6].
